name: Digispark ATtiny85 USB
description: The $1.50-2 USB-stick ATtiny85 board with the Micronucleus bootloader: plug into any USB-A port, no programmer needed; ideal for tiny USB gadgets, 5 usable I/O and about 6 KB of flash.
notes: Micronucleus USB bootloader (software USB, V-USB): uploads via micronucleus/Arduino with no programmer, ~6 KB usable flash, bootloader waits ~5 s after plug-in.
P0-P5 are GPIO but P3/P4 are the USB lines and P5 is RESET; using P5 as GPIO needs the RSTDISBL fuse (removes the ability to reflash). In practice 5 usable pins.
Many clones ship with weak USB regulators/zeners and need a short USB extension to enumerate reliably. Micro-USB versions exist. Dimensions approximate.
digistump.com was unreachable when this was checked; the Arduino core is on GitHub.
